lede: The biggest thing on the table this week is Monday's Norwood Planning and Zoning meeting, where commissioners are set to vote on adopting Phase I of a full Land Use Code rewrite — the kind of decision that quietly sets the rules for development and density for years to come. Tuesday brings a heavy Town Council agenda, including public hearings on converting two affordable units at 215 East Colorado from price-capped ownership to employee dwelling units. The county also holds a continued public hearing Tuesday on adopting new International Building Codes and a low-carbon energy code that would affect every construction project in San Miguel County.

notable.stake: Vote on Ordinance adopting Norwood's Land Use Code rewrite — sets future development rules.
Board votes on resolutions supporting Prop NN and Amendment 87, plus second-reading policy approvals.
Resolution to convert two affordable ownership units to EDUs, removing the maximum sale price cap.
Public hearings on deed-restriction conversion removing price caps on two town affordable units.
Commission weighing six leak forgiveness requests and a new leak-check fee for Norwood water customers.
Continued public hearing on adopting new International Building Codes countywide; 2027 nonprofit funding.
